text:
Alex: FYI CI size gate tripped on the new fused-attn kernels after landing the attention-optimizer RFC. Seeing ~+28% fatbin size on the nvcc build compared to previous commit. Anyone seen this pattern before?
CI-bot: build #432 — artifact size increased 3.2MB (threshold 1.0MB). logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/432/artifacts
Maria: can you paste the nvcc commandline and gencode list? my hunch is we're shipping too many cubins/PTX for supported SMs.
Alex: pasted the command we used:
```
nvcc -O3 -Xptxas=-v \
  -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 \
  -gencode arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 \
  -gencode arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 \
  -rdc=true -lineinfo -Xlinker --gc-sections -o libkernels.fatbin
```
we added sm_90 because of some internal infra nodes, but left 80/86 for broader compatibility.
Chao: sm_90 brings a large PTX/cubin payload. nvcc emits PTX+COBIN per -gencode entry. Options: a) reduce gencode list to the concrete SMs we actively run in CI/dedicated, b) compile PTX-only (code=compute_90) so the runtime can JIT to cubin on target GPUs, c) try -Xcompiler flags to reduce sections, d) try stripping symbols and lto tweaks.
Sam: important runtime constraint: our serving runtime currently prefers loading prebuilt cubins for speed. If we switch to shipping PTX-only for some arches we need to ensure the runtime can JIT/compile or fall back to a compatible cubin variant. That implies runtime changes and a migration plan.
Maria: CI short-term: add per-arch size breakdown. We can extract with cuobjdump/cuda-nvlink (cuobjdump -ptx -cubin) and compute sizes per SM/PTX vs cubin. Add a diff check so any single-kernel increase > 1MB triggers a human review.
Alex: also noticing nvlink output explodes when -rdc=true (device code linking). Splitting kernels into separate object builds and doing a targeted link may keep unrelated symbols out of the final fatbin. Old toolchain had split-object artifacts for that reason.
Chao: quick mitigation proposal: 1) remove sm_90 from default gencode in the main build (keep it in a separate compat build) 2) add an extraction step in CI that runs cuobjdump and uploads per-kernel sizes as metadata 3) add compressed artifact uploads and gate on both uncompressed and compressed sizes so we can spot regressions even after compression. I'll prototype a script.
Sam: action items: Chao -> prototype cuobjdump extraction script and PR for eng-runtime/ci; Sam -> add size-gate job and configure thresholds; Alex -> open a small RFC for runtime PTX fallback support (what APIs we need, compile-on-load perf regression numbers). ETA: end of week for prototypes.
Lisa: small note — some of the quantized kernels change __ldg/shared usage and that affects codegen size significantly. Worth adding a test that compares kernel IR or objdump diffs for quant builds separately.
Alex: agreed. If we go the PTX-fallback route we should only do it for a targeted whitelist of kernels (attn fused, matmul kernels) to limit runtime JIT surface area.
Maria: also consider build flags: --fatbin-options or nvcc `-Xfatbin` options? and double-check -lineinfo vs -g (we may not need line info in prod builds).
Sam: one more pragmatic option — keep full gencode in a debug/compat build but strip to a minimal gencode in the release artifact that we ship to dedicated/runtime. That buys safety while keeping the release bin small.
Alex: sounds good. I'll file the runtime RFC and add notes about a phased rollout + canary on dedicated pools. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
CI-bot: Re-run queued after PRs land.
